Terminal adstock state

Source: R/adstock.R
adstock_state.Rd

Returns the carryover left in flight at the end of a series, in a form adstock_geometric() and friends accept as their state argument. This is how you continue a filter across contiguous chunks of a series without re-running it from the beginning. step_adstock() computes it at prep() time and reports it through tidy().

Usage

adstock_state(
  x,
  decay,
  max_lag = Inf,
  state = 0,
  by = NULL,
  na_action = c("error", "zero", "keep"),
  missing_state = c("error", "cold")
)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of media spend (or impressions, or GRPs) in time order. x must already be sorted by time and evenly spaced; the function has no index argument and cannot check this for you. Use step_adstock() if you want the time index validated. Infinite values are an error, since the filter would carry them into later periods; missing values are handled by na_action.

decay

Geometric decay coefficient in [0, 1]. Required for the infinite kernel. A finite kernel's state is the tail of x and does not depend on the decay, so there decay can be left out.

max_lag

Number of periods the kernel spans. Inf, the default, gives the recursive form, whose state is a single number.

state

Carryover already in flight at the start of x, for chaining calls across contiguous chunks of a series. The default 0 is a cold start, meaning no media ran before x began. For the infinite kernel this is a single number, the raw (unnormalised) accumulator; for a finite max_lag it is the max_lag - 1 values that came before x, oldest first. Obtain it from adstock_state(), which records the max_lag (and, for the infinite kernel, the decay) it was computed for, so that a state from another kernel is refused rather than used. A plain numeric vector of the right length is accepted too.

When by is supplied, pass either the scalar 0 (or NULL) to cold-start every group, or a named list with one entry per group, which is the shape adstock_state() returns when it is given by. A list with a NULL entry is an error rather than a silent cold start for that group.

by

Optional grouping vector, or data frame of grouping vectors, the same length as x. Adstock is applied independently within each group, which is what geo-level and panel models need. Never rely on dplyr::group_by() for this: grouping metadata does not reliably survive into every context where this function is called. Missing values are an error, in a vector or in any column of a data frame.

na_action

What to do about missing values in x. "error" (the default) refuses to guess. "zero" treats missing media as no media, which is usually right for spend but is a substantive assumption. "keep" lets NA propagate through the filter, which for the recursive form poisons every subsequent value.

missing_state

What to do when state is a per-group list with no entry for a group in by. "error" (the default) refuses; "cold" cold-starts those groups, as step_adstock() does by default for groups it did not see at prep() time.

Value

An object of class mm_adstock_state, a numeric vector that records what it was computed for. For the infinite kernel it holds a single number, the raw (unnormalised) accumulator, and records the kernel, max_lag and decay. For a finite max_lag it holds the last max_lag - 1 values of the series, oldest first, and records max_lag; when x is shorter than that, the earlier values come from state, or are zeros from a cold start. When by is supplied, a named list of such objects, one per group, in order of first appearance.

Details

The stored state is always in raw units, independent of normalise, so a state captured under one normalisation setting stays valid under the other.

The transforms check a state against their own arguments and refuse one computed for another kernel, instead of starting from the wrong carryover. The recursive accumulator is valid only for the same decay and max_lag = Inf. A finite state is the raw tail of the series, so it serves every kernel with the same max_lag: adstock_weibull(), adstock_delayed() and adstock_filter() accept it as readily as adstock_geometric(). A plain numeric vector is still accepted and is checked only for its length and for missing or infinite values.

For the recursive kernel this object is one double per series, so continuing the filter needs none of the earlier observations. step_adstock() stores the training media as well, so that bake() can also take new data that repeats training periods; see its Storage section.

See also

adstock_geometric(), adstock_weibull(), adstock_filter(), and step_adstock(), which reports this state through tidy().

Examples

first_half <- c(100, 80, 60, 40)
second_half <- c(20, 10, 5, 0)

s <- adstock_state(first_half, decay = 0.5)
s
#> <adstock state: geometric accumulator at decay 0.5>
#> [1] 102.5

# Filtering in two chunks with the state carried across gives exactly the
# same answer as filtering the whole series at once
chunked <- c(
  adstock_geometric(first_half, decay = 0.5),
  adstock_geometric(second_half, decay = 0.5, state = s)
)
whole <- adstock_geometric(c(first_half, second_half), decay = 0.5)
all.equal(chunked, whole)
#> [1] TRUE

# A state from another kernel is refused
try(adstock_geometric(second_half, decay = 0.5, max_lag = 2, state = s))
#> Error in adstock_geometric(second_half, decay = 0.5, max_lag = 2, state = s) : 
#>   `state` was computed for a different kernel length.
#> ✖ It is the state of a kernel with `max_lag = Inf`; this call uses `max_lag =
#>   2`.
#> ℹ Recompute it with `adstock_state()` and the same `max_lag`.
